title: .respawnpack/runtime/rollover/<host>-<conversationId>/cycle.json — the machine's current context-cycle identity
description: Written by core/lifecycle/cycle.js's persist(), called from core/lifecycle/machine.js on mint (first open) and on every advance (a successful verify-identity). A CONTEXT CYCLE is the work performed between two compactions — NOT a session, because a compacted conversation keeps its session id, which is exactly why a v0.2 latch keyed on session id fired once and went silent forever. This file is a FAST PATH and a CROSS-CHECK ONLY: the journal (rollover-journal family) is the authority, and machine.open() REWRITES this file from the journal's fold whenever the two disagree — a crash between the journal append and this file's write is the one case where they legitimately do, for one open(). GITIGNORED, machine-local. No schemaVersion: this record is re-minted with a fresh nonce on every advance and re-derived from the journal on every restart, so there is no format for an old reader to disagree about.

conversationId.description: The host's own stable conversation identity, VERBATIM and un-sanitized — this is what an identity-verification record compares against, and is why it is kept separately from the sanitized directory-name segment derived from it.

index.description: 0-based, monotone, incremented exactly once per OBSERVED compaction completion (inside verify-identity).

nonce.description: 12 hex characters, minted fresh with the cycle. What makes reuse of an index DETECTABLE — an artifact bound to cycle N carries N's nonce, so a re-minted N after a crash cannot silently adopt the orphaned cycle's latches or receipts.

provenance.description: Why this record has the index it has — 'cycle 0 because this is the first cycle' and 'cycle 0 because the journal was gone' are different facts. 'minted-after-repair' names the second explicitly rather than letting a reader infer it from the index alone.

cycleId.description: host:conversationId:index:nonce — the composite identity every latch and every handoff's contextCycleId is keyed on.
